html:
The Warekena are an Arawakan people of the Xié River, a branch of the upper Rio Negro in Brazil, with a group in Venezuela.

They traditionally spoke Warekena but today mostly speak Nheengatu, a Tupi based common language that Carmelite missionaries spread along the Rio Negro in the colonial era. They fish, farm manioc and hunt. Portuguese slave raids and later the rubber trade drew many into forced labour. Their Arawakan neighbours include the Baniwa, the Kuripako and the Tariana.
sum: The Warekena are an Arawakan people of the Xié River, a branch of the upper Rio Negro in Brazil, with a group in Venezuela.
